name: Albertonykus
sum: Small alvarezsaurid from the Maastrichtian Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, found in an Albertosaurus bonebed.
holotype: Forelimb and hind-limb bones from the Albertosaurus bonebed at the top of Unit 4, Horseshoe Canyon Formation, Dry Island Provincial Park, Alberta.
material: Fore- and hind-limb remains of several individuals.
biology: Its forelimbs seem built for digging but too short for burrowing, so it is thought to have opened wood-nesting termite colonies.
author: Longrich and Currie 2009

sources.text: N. R. Longrich and P. J. Currie. 2009. Albertonykus borealis, a new alvarezsaur (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Early Maastrichtian of Alberta, Canada: implications for the systematics and ecology of the Alvarezsauridae. Cretaceous Research 30(1):239-252
